content: The Health Resources & Services Administration (HRSA) and the World Health Organization (WHO) provide treatment guidelines regarding the interactions of rifampin with various drugs. 1. Rifampin and Artemether/Lumefantrine: Rifampin reduces the effectiveness of artemether/lumefantrine by inducing the CYP3A4 enzyme, leading to decreased serum concentrations and loss of antimalarial efficacy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 2. Rifampin and Atazanavir: Rifampin increases the metabolism of atazanavir, significantly reducing its levels and antiviral efficacy. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of viral resistance. 3. Rifampin and Bictegravir: Rifampin induces CYP3A4 and UGT1A1 enzymes, leading to a substantial reduction in bictegravir plasma concentrations. This may result in therapeutic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 4. Rifampin and Cabotegravir: Co-administration is contraindicated. 5. Rifampin and Cariprazine: Rifampin induces CYP3A4, reducing cariprazine levels and its active metabolites. The interaction has not been fully evaluated, but co-administration is contraindicated. 6. Rifampin and Cobicistat: Rifampin induces CYP3A4, reducing cobicistat levels and risking therapeutic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 7. Rifampin and Cobimetinib: Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Rifampin and Darunavir: Rifampin induces CYP3A4, reducing darunavir levels and risking loss of antiviral efficacy and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Rifampin and Doravirine: Rifampin induces CYP3A4, reducing doravirine plasma concentrations and risking virologic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Rifampin and Elbasvir/Grazoprevir: Rifampin induces CYP3A4, reducing the therapeutic effect of elbasvir/grazoprevir. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Rifampin and Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: Rifampin induces CYP3A4, reducing plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and associated drugs, risking virologic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Rifampin and Etravirine: Rifampin increases the metabolism of etravirine, reducing its levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 13. Rifampin and Fostemsavir: Rifampin induces CYP3A4, significantly reducing the active moiety of fostemsavir, leading to virologic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 14. Rifampin and Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Rifampin induces CYP3A4 and P-gp, reducing glecaprevir/pibrentasvir plasma concentrations and efficacy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Rifampin and Irinotecan: Rifampin induces CYP2B6, reducing irinotecan levels and efficacy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 16. Rifampin and Isavuconazonium Sulfate: Rifampin induces CYP3A4, reducing isavuconazonium sulfate levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Rifampin and Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir: Rifampin induces P-gp, reducing sofosbuvir levels and its active metabolite, leading to therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 18. Rifampin and Lenacapavir: Rifampin induces CYP3A4, reducing lenacapavir levels and risking virologic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Rifampin and Naloxegol: Rifampin induces CYP3A4, reducing naloxegol levels. Co-administration is not recommended. 22. Rifampin and Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir: Rifampin induces CYP3A4, significantly reducing nirmatrelvir levels, risking virologic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 23.
